metadata.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
metadata.authors: H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Aguera y Arcas

nodes.name: Federated Learning
nodes.statement_latex: A decentralized learning approach in which a shared model is trained by a loose federation of participating devices (\emph{clients}) coordinated by a central \emph{server}; each client holds a local training dataset that is never uploaded, and only model updates are communicated.
nodes.statement_clean: Decentralized model training where clients keep raw data local and only share model updates with a central server.

nodes.name: Federated Optimization Setting
nodes.statement_latex: The optimization regime arising from federated learning, characterized by four properties: (i) Non-IID per-client data, (ii) unbalanced local dataset sizes, (iii) massively distributed clients (number of clients $\gg$ examples per client), and (iv) limited communication.
nodes.statement_clean: Distributed optimization characterized by non-IID, unbalanced, massively distributed data and limited communication.

nodes.name: Client Data Partition
nodes.statement_latex: There are $K$ clients indexed by $k$. Client $k$ holds the index set $\mathcal{P}_k$ with $n_k = |\mathcal{P}_k|$ examples; the partition $\{\mathcal{P}_k\}_{k=1}^K$ covers $\{1,\dots,n\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The training set is partitioned across K clients, with client k holding $n_k$ examples indexed by $\mathcal{P}_k$.

nodes.name: Local Objective $F_k$
nodes.statement_latex: $F_k(w) = \frac{1}{n_k} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{P}_k} f_i(w)$, the average per-example loss over client $k$'s local data.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-client average loss on its local dataset.

nodes.name: IID vs. Non-IID Partition
nodes.statement_latex: If $\mathcal{P}_k$ is formed by uniform random assignment, then $\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{P}_k}[F_k(w)] = f(w)$ (the IID assumption). The \emph{non-IID} setting drops this assumption: $F_k$ may be an arbitrarily bad approximation to $f$.
nodes.statement_clean: IID means each client's local objective equals the global objective in expectation; non-IID drops this assumption.

nodes.name: Expected Local Updates per Round $u$
nodes.statement_latex: $u = (\mathbb{E}[n_k] / B) \cdot E = nE/(KB)$, the expected number of SGD updates a client performs per communication round.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected number of local SGD steps a client performs each communication round, parameterized by E, B, K, n.

nodes.name: MNIST Non-IID Pathological Partition
nodes.statement_latex: Sort MNIST by digit label, divide into 200 shards of size 300, and assign each of 100 clients 2 shards. Each client typically holds examples of only two digits.
nodes.statement_clean: Pathological non-IID MNIST split: each of 100 clients gets 2 shards (~600 examples) drawn from at most 2 digit classes.

nodes.name: Shakespeare Per-Role Client Dataset
nodes.statement_latex: From \emph{The Complete Works of William Shakespeare}, build one client per speaking role with at least two lines (1146 clients). For each client, the first 80\% of lines form the training set and the last 20\% the test set.
nodes.statement_clean: Shakespeare client split: one client per speaking role (1146 clients), with a temporal 80/20 train/test split per client.

nodes.name: Federated Finite-Sum Optimization Problem
nodes.statement_latex: $\min_{w \in \mathbb{R}^d} f(w) \quad \text{where} \quad f(w) \eqdef \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(w) = \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{n_k}{n} F_k(w)$, with $f_i(w) = \ell(x_i, y_i; w)$ in the supervised case, optimized over data partitioned across $K$ clients.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize a finite-sum loss whose terms are partitioned across K clients, subject to communication constraints.

nodes.name: FedSGD Server Aggregation Update
nodes.statement_latex: $w_{t+1} \leftarrow w_t - \eta \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{n_k}{n} g_k$, where $g_k = \nabla F_k(w_t)$ and $\sum_k \frac{n_k}{n} g_k = \nabla f(w_t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Server applies a weighted-average gradient step to the global model.

nodes.name: FedSGD Equivalent Model-Average Form
nodes.statement_latex: $\forall k,\; w_{t+1}^k \leftarrow w_t - \eta g_k; \quad w_{t+1} \leftarrow \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{n_k}{n} w_{t+1}^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Equivalent rewrite: each client takes one local SGD step, then the server averages the resulting models.

nodes.name: FedAvg Iterated Local Update
nodes.statement_latex: $w^k \leftarrow w^k - \eta \nabla F_k(w^k)$ iterated multiple times before the averaging step; this is the local-update primitive of \algfont{FedAvg}.
nodes.statement_clean: Each client iterates local SGD updates several times before the server averages.

nodes.name: FedSGD (Federated SGD baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Baseline algorithm: each round selects a $C$-fraction of clients and computes a single full-batch gradient $g_k = \nabla F_k(w_t)$, which the server aggregates as $w_{t+1} \leftarrow w_t - \eta \sum_k \frac{n_k}{n} g_k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Large-batch synchronous SGD baseline that uses one client-side gradient per round.

nodes.name: FederatedAveraging (FedAvg)
nodes.statement_latex: Each round, the server samples a random fraction $C$ of $K$ clients and broadcasts $w_t$; each selected client runs $E$ local epochs of minibatch SGD with batch size $B$ on its local data, then returns $w_{t+1}^k$; the server forms $w_{t+1} \leftarrow \sum_{k \in S_t} (n_k / m_t) w_{t+1}^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Synchronous federated optimizer that combines local minibatch SGD on each sampled client with weighted server-side model averaging.

nodes.name: Initialize global model
nodes.statement_latex: Server initializes $w_0$.

nodes.name: Sample client subset $S_t$
nodes.statement_latex: At round $t$, set $m \leftarrow \max(C \cdot K, 1)$ and draw $S_t$ as a random set of $m$ clients.

nodes.name: Parallel ClientUpdate calls
nodes.statement_latex: For each $k \in S_t$ in parallel, compute $w_{t+1}^k \leftarrow \text{ClientUpdate}(k, w_t)$.

nodes.name: Aggregate by weighted model averaging
nodes.statement_latex: Set $m_t \leftarrow \sum_{k \in S_t} n_k$ and $w_{t+1} \leftarrow \sum_{k \in S_t} \frac{n_k}{m_t} w_{t+1}^k$ (the corrected per-erratum form).

nodes.name: ClientUpdate: local minibatch SGD
nodes.statement_latex: Split $\mathcal{P}_k$ into batches of size $B$; for each local epoch $i = 1,\dots,E$ and each batch $b$, set $w \leftarrow w - \eta \nabla \ell(w; b)$; return $w$ to the server.

nodes.name: MNIST 2NN model
nodes.statement_latex: A simple multilayer perceptron with 2 hidden layers of 200 ReLU units (199{,}210 parameters) trained on MNIST as the \tnn baseline.

nodes.name: MNIST CNN model
nodes.statement_latex: A CNN with two 5x5 conv layers (32 then 64 channels, each with 2x2 max pooling), a 512-unit ReLU FC layer, and a softmax output (1{,}663{,}370 parameters), trained on MNIST.

nodes.name: Shakespeare character LSTM
nodes.statement_latex: A stacked character-level LSTM that embeds characters into 8 dimensions, processes them through 2 LSTM layers of 256 nodes, and outputs a softmax over characters (866{,}578 parameters), trained on the per-role Shakespeare client dataset with unroll length 80.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 CNN experiment
nodes.statement_latex: On CIFAR-10 partitioned IID over 100 clients (500 train / 100 test each), \fedavgshort with $C=0.1$, $E=5$, $B=50$ reaches 85\% test accuracy in 2{,}000 rounds versus $\sim$197{,}500 minibatch updates for sequential SGD baseline.

nodes.name: Large-scale word-level LSTM (social-network posts)
nodes.statement_latex: A 256-node word LSTM over a 10{,}000-word vocabulary (4{,}950{,}544 parameters) trained on 10 million social-network posts grouped by author into 500{,}000+ clients; $\fedavgshort$ ($\eta=9.0$) reaches 10.5\% accuracy in 35 rounds versus 820 rounds for $\fedsgdshort$ ($23\times$ fewer).

nodes.name: Two-MNIST-models parameter-averaging illustration (Figure 1)
nodes.statement_latex: Two MNIST \tnn models $w, w'$ trained by SGD on disjoint 600-example subsets are averaged as $\theta w + (1-\theta) w'$ for $\theta \in [-0.2, 1.2]$. With independent random initialization the averaged model is much worse; with a shared random initialization, $\tfrac{1}{2} w + \tfrac{1}{2} w'$ achieves significantly lower loss than either parent.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical illustration that parameter averaging works well only when the two models share an initialization.

nodes.name: Communication is the dominant cost
nodes.statement_latex: In federated optimization, communication costs dominate (clients limited to $\le 1$ MB/s upload), so the design goal is to use additional client computation to reduce the number of communication rounds.

nodes.name: Erratum on aggregation weights
nodes.statement_latex: Earlier versions of the paper incorrectly indicated summation over all $K$ clients in the aggregation; the corrected form sums only over the sampled set $S_t$ with weights $n_k / m_t$ where $m_t = \sum_{k \in S_t} n_k$.

nodes.name: Implicit regularization conjecture
nodes.statement_latex: $\fedavgshort$ converges to higher test accuracy than $\fedsgdshort$ on all three model classes; the authors conjecture model averaging provides a regularization benefit similar to dropout.

nodes.name: Decay $E$ in late training
nodes.section: 3 Experimental Results (Can we over-optimize on the client datasets?)
nodes.statement_latex: For some models (notably the Shakespeare LSTM), very large $E$ causes $\fedavgshort$ to plateau or diverge; the authors suggest decaying local computation per round (smaller $E$ or larger $B$) analogously to learning-rate decay.

nodes.name: Privacy via update minimality and data-processing inequality
nodes.statement_latex: Federated updates are the minimal information needed to improve the model; by the data-processing inequality they contain no more information than the raw data, and typically much less.

nodes.name: Differentially private and SMPC-secure FedAvg
nodes.statement_latex: Provide stronger formal privacy guarantees for $\fedavgshort$ via differential privacy, secure multi-party computation, or their combination — open as future work in this paper.

nodes.name: Convergence theory for FedAvg on non-IID data
nodes.statement_latex: The paper provides no convergence proof; characterizing when iterated local SGD plus model averaging converges (especially for non-convex objectives on non-IID, unbalanced clients) is left open.

nodes.name: One-shot model averaging (cited baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Each client locally minimizes (possibly regularized) loss on its data; resulting models are averaged once to produce the global model. In the worst case (convex, IID setting), the resulting global model is no better than a model trained on a single client.
nodes.origin_citation: Zhang et al. 2012 (zhang12communication); Arjevani & Shamir 2015; Zinkevich et al. 2010

nodes.name: Asynchronous distributed SGD (cited baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Asynchronous parameter-server SGD applied to deep network training; requires a prohibitive number of updates in the federated setting.

nodes.name: Iterative local-model averaging (cited prior)
nodes.statement_latex: Distributed training by iteratively averaging locally trained models, previously studied for the perceptron and for speech-recognition DNNs in the data-center setting (\le 16 workers, IID).
nodes.origin_citation: McDonald et al. 2010; Povey et al. 2015; Zhang et al. 2015 (elastic averaging)
